sections.h2: Why is Walton County one of the fastest changing counties east of Atlanta?
sections.html:
Walton County sits about 30 miles east of Atlanta in the Georgia Piedmont, and its population keeps climbing as Atlanta's suburbs push outward. The Census Bureau counted 83,768 residents in 2010, 96,673 in 2020 and estimates 112,696 for July 2025, per QuickFacts.

The county was created in 1818 and carries the name of George Walton, one of the three Georgia signers of the Declaration of Independence. Monroe is the county seat and largest city, Loganville is the other major city, and Social Circle, Between and Good Hope round out the municipal map, according to Wikipedia. Land totals 330 square miles, with Barrow, Oconee, Morgan, Newton, Rockdale and Gwinnett counties on its borders.

Most of the county is served by the Walton County School District, while Social Circle has its own city school system. Public high schools include Loganville, Monroe Area and Walnut Grove.

The numbers behind that growth are steep: 60,687 people in 2000, 83,768 in 2010 and 96,673 in 2020. A six-member commission elected from single-member districts, with a chairman chosen countywide, passes county law and sets the county share of the tax levy.

sections.h2: What do Census numbers say about Walton County housing?
sections.html:
Walton County is a homeowner county with prices close to the national median. QuickFacts lists a median owner-occupied value of $339,500 for 2020-2024, against $332,700 for the nation.

  • Owner-occupied housing unit rate: 79.3%, compared with 65.2% nationally.
  • Median gross rent: $1,175.
  • Median household income: $84,945.
  • Households: 35,755, and housing units: 39,911 as of July 1, 2025.
  • Building permits issued in 2025: 569.

Fast growth and a high ownership rate mean a seller often competes with new construction on the edges of Monroe and Loganville. Against that new supply, a house that needs work or carries back taxes is easier to sell to a buyer who accepts it as-is.

sections.h2: Who sends the Walton County tax bill?
sections.html:
The Walton County Tax Commissioner sends one bill, and for Monroe owners it includes the city's share. Monroe stopped billing its own property tax in 2016 and folded it into the county statement, due on the county's date.

  • Main office: 303 S. Hammond Drive, Suite 100, Monroe, GA 30655, open Monday to Friday 8:30 a.m. to 4:45 p.m.
  • Property tax phone: (770) 266-1736. Email: WCTC@co.walton.ga.us.
  • Tax Assessors' Office, same address: (770) 267-1352, for returns, values and exemptions.
  • Online search and payment through the Walton County Tax Commissioner site.

The county's own page says the bill reflects the owner of record on January 1. Mortgage lenders usually pay from escrow, but the homeowner remains responsible for seeing that the payment is made. The office mails the bill only to the January 1 owner, so a new homeowner should send a copy to the lender.

Churches, nonprofit hospitals and public property may be exempt, though the Board of Tax Assessors must approve the status before liability comes off, and the request is due by April 1.

sections.h2: What is the Walton County tax calendar and penalty schedule?
sections.html:
Bills go out in late August and the due date is November 15. After that the balance picks up interest each month, plus the fees and penalties in the table below.

Walton County property tax calendar and delinquency steps (Tax Commissioner site)
StepWhat the county says
January 1 to April 1File returns and homestead applications with the Tax Assessors
Late AugustReal and personal property bills mailed
November 15Payment due; later balances accrue monthly interest
90 days past dueFi.Fa. lien fee of $20.50 on bills under $100, $30.50 on bills over $100
Every 120 days5% penalty on the remaining balance, up to 20%

Before a lien is issued the office sends a 30-day notice of intent. A Fi.Fa. is recorded on the General Execution Docket at the Clerk of Superior Court and stays in effect seven years. Partial payments are accepted, though interest and penalties keep running on what is left.

sections.h2: How do appeals, returns and exemptions work in Walton County?
sections.html:
The appeal window is 45 days from the mailing date of the assessment notice, with the appeal sent to the Board of Tax Assessors. If no agreement is reached, the county's page says the file is forwarded automatically to the Board of Equalization.

A taxpayer who disputes value can also file a return between January 1 and April 1 stating what they believe the fair market value is. Failure to file a required return carries a 10% penalty on the value not returned. Mobile and modular homes get two chances to contest value, once during the return period and again within 45 days of the bill, which is usually mailed in January.

  • Homestead applications go to the Tax Assessors' Office, with April 1 the cutoff or the last day to appeal the assessment notice.
  • Owners 65 and older receive an exemption from Walton County School District tax on the house and one acre.
  • Owners 70 and older get an exemption of up to $30,000 on land above one acre.
  • A PT-61 transfer form filed with the Clerk of Superior Court can stand in for a return when the property was not changed.

Personal property returns, such as business equipment, are due every year by April 1 with the Tax Assessors, and the county charges a 10% penalty for failing to file or filing late. A refund claim for tax paid in error must be made in writing to the board of commissioners within three years of payment, and it has to rest on an error, not a disagreement about value.

sections.h2: How do I handle Walton County tax when I sell?
sections.html:
Send the closing statement to the Tax Commissioner as soon as you close. The office asks for a copy by email to WCTC@co.walton.ga.us or fax to (770) 267-1416, and it can then mail a duplicate bill in the new owner's name when the purchase happened before November 15 of that tax year.

Ask for a written payoff before closing so the title company can pay the year's bill and any older balance out of your proceeds. If a lien has already been recorded, paying the tax with its fees, penalties and interest cancels the Fi.Fa. The county does not hand its liens to bulk investors, and any tax sale takes place in front of the Walton County Government Building on the first Tuesday of the month after newspaper notice.

A sale to a buyer who takes the house as-is can close around these items without repair requests, which suits an inherited or rental house with several years open.

faqs.q: When are Walton County property taxes due?
faqs.a: November 15, with bills mailed in late August. Taxes unpaid after that date are delinquent and carry monthly interest, and a 5% penalty is added every 120 days up to 20%.

faqs.q: What number do I call for a Walton County property tax question?
faqs.a: Call (770) 266-1736 for the Tax Commissioner's property tax desk. Questions about value, returns and exemptions go to the Tax Assessors' Office at (770) 267-1352.

faqs.q: How long do I have to appeal a Walton County assessment?
faqs.a: You have 45 days from the date the assessment notice was mailed. File with the Board of Tax Assessors, and an unresolved appeal is passed on to the Board of Equalization.

faqs.q: Does the City of Monroe send its own tax bill?
faqs.a: No. Since 2016 the Walton County Tax Commissioner issues one consolidated bill that includes Monroe city tax. Older balances from 2015 and earlier are paid at Monroe City Hall.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Walton County house that has a tax lien?
faqs.a: Yes. Pay the outstanding tax, fees, penalties and interest at or before closing, and the Fi.Fa. is cancelled. Request a written payoff from the Tax Commissioner so the closing agent has the exact figure.
